title: PostgreSQL
overview: PostgreSQL is the most feature-complete open-source relational database in the world. It runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux, stores structured rows plus JSONB documents, geospatial data (PostGIS), and full-text search, all with strict ACID guarantees. It is the default choice for new applications that need real SQL correctness without licensing costs.

demo.how_to_run: psql -h localhost -U postgres -f demo.sql  (or paste into pgAdmin / psql prompt)

features: JSONB document storage with GIN indexing
Advanced SQL: CTEs, window functions, recursive queries
Logical and physical replication, point-in-time recovery
dialect_notes: Very close to standard SQL. Auto-increment: SERIAL or GENERATED ... AS IDENTITY. RETURNING clause returns inserted rows. Casts use :: (e.g. price::numeric). Case-insensitive match: ILIKE. True boolean type; arrays and JSON operators (->, ->>).
when_to_use: General application backend needing correct transactions
Any project where MySQL quirks would hurt
when_not_to_use: Trivial single-file app — SQLite is lighter
Extreme write sharding without an operator — consider CockroachDB/YugabyteDB

install.macos: brew install postgresql@18 && brew services start postgresql@18
install.windows: Download the EDB installer from postgresql.org

provenance: Public record of a real database engine; facts fact-checked against vendor documentation.

title: MySQL
overview: MySQL is the world’s most deployed open-source relational database, powering a huge share of the web including WordPress. The default InnoDB storage engine gives ACID transactions, crash recovery, and foreign keys. Version 8 brought window functions, CTEs, and a real JSON type, closing most of the gap with PostgreSQL.

demo.how_to_run: mysql -u root -p < demo.sql  (or paste into MySQL Workbench)

features: InnoDB: ACID transactions, row-level locking, crash recovery
Replication: async, semi-sync, and Group Replication
JSON data type with generated-column indexing
MySQL Shell, Router, and Workbench tooling
dialect_notes: Auto-increment: AUTO_INCREMENT column attribute. String quoting with backticks for identifiers. LIMIT n OFFSET m instead of FETCH FIRST. No FULL OUTER JOIN (emulate with UNION). Functions differ: NOW(), CONCAT(), IFNULL(). Boolean is TINYINT(1) alias.
when_to_use: WordPress / PHP stacks and LAMP hosting
Read-heavy web apps with simple schemas
Environments where operators already know MySQL
when_not_to_use: Complex analytics or CTE-heavy queries — PostgreSQL reads better

install.macos: brew install mysql && brew services start mysql
install.windows: Download the MySQL Installer from dev.mysql.com

provenance: Public record of a real database engine; facts fact-checked against vendor documentation.

title: MariaDB
overview: MariaDB is the community fork of MySQL created by MySQL’s founder after Oracle’s acquisition. It stays wire-compatible with MySQL while adding its own engines (Aria, ColumnStore, Spider), the Galera multi-primary cluster, and faster release cadence. Most MySQL applications run unchanged on MariaDB.

demo.how_to_run: mariadb -u root -p < demo.sql  (or paste into DBeaver / HeidiSQL)

features: Galera Cluster: true multi-primary synchronous replication
ColumnStore for analytics, Spider for sharding
dialect_notes: Same dialect as MySQL plus extras: sequences (CREATE SEQUENCE), INTERSECT/EXCEPT set ops, window functions, JSON functions, and system-versioned (temporal) tables via WITH SYSTEM VERSIONING.
when_to_use: MySQL-compatible app that wants open governance
Multi-primary write clusters without extra licensing
Mixed OLTP + light analytics on one server
when_not_to_use: You need Oracle’s MySQL Enterprise support contracts
Exotic MySQL 8.4-only features — check parity first

install.macos: brew install mariadb && brew services start mariadb
install.windows: Download the MSI installer from mariadb.org

provenance: Public record of a real database engine; facts fact-checked against vendor documentation.

title: SQLite
overview: SQLite is a complete SQL database engine in a single C library — no server, no setup, the whole database is one file on disk. It is the most deployed database software on Earth: inside every phone, browser, and airplane system. Perfect for apps, prototypes, tests, and edge devices.

demo.how_to_run: sqlite3 shop.db < demo.sql  — the shop.db file IS the database

platforms: Everywhere: embedded in apps, phones, browsers
features: Serverless: database is a single cross-platform file
ACID transactions, WAL mode for concurrent readers
dialect_notes: Dynamic typing with type affinity. Auto-increment: INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT. No RIGHT/FULL OUTER JOIN. ALTER TABLE historically limited (modern versions improved). UPSERT: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE. Concatenation uses ||.
when_not_to_use: Many concurrent writers — use client/server Postgres
Central database shared across a network

install.windows: Download the sqlite-tools zip from sqlite.org
install.python: import sqlite3  # built into Python — no install needed

provenance: Public record of a real database engine; facts fact-checked against vendor documentation.

title: Microsoft SQL Server
overview: SQL Server is Microsoft’s enterprise relational database, dominant in Windows-centric companies. T-SQL is a rich dialect with window functions, MERGE, and deep integration with .NET, Excel, and Power BI. The Linux edition and a free Developer/Express edition make it accessible outside pure-Windows shops.

demo.how_to_run: sqlcmd -S localhost -U sa -P <password> -i demo.sql  (or paste into SSMS / Azure Data Studio)

features: Always On availability groups and failover clustering
Temporal tables, JSON support, in-memory OLTP
dialect_notes: Auto-increment: IDENTITY(1,1). Pagination: OFFSET n ROWS FETCH NEXT m ROWS ONLY, or TOP n. Identifiers in [brackets]. Concatenation with +. ISNULL() instead of COALESCE shorthand; GETDATE() for now. Schema prefix dbo. is conventional.
when_to_use: Enterprise reporting with Power BI / SSRS
Workloads needing Always On HA on Windows
when_not_to_use: Small Linux shops — PostgreSQL is simpler

install.windows: Download SQL Server 2022/2025 Express or Developer from microsoft.com
install.linux_ubuntu: Follow the mssql-server apt repo guide, then: sudo /opt/mssql/bin/mssql-conf setup

provenance: Public record of a real database engine; facts fact-checked against vendor documentation.

title: Oracle Database
overview: Oracle Database is the long-reigning enterprise RDBMS — the system banks, telcos, and governments trust for the workloads that must never be wrong. Oracle 23ai adds AI vector search and JSON-relational duality to the classic engine. Power comes with complexity and the industry’s most expensive licensing.

demo.how_to_run: sqlplus system/<password>@localhost/FREEPDB1 @demo.sql  (or paste into SQL Developer)

features: Maximum-availability architecture: RAC, Data Guard, RMAN
PL/SQL: the most capable procedural SQL
JSON-relational duality views, AI vector search (23ai)
Fine-grained security: VPD, label security, TDE
Partitioning, advanced compression, in-memory column store
dialect_notes: Classic: sequences + triggers for auto-increment (23ai adds identity columns). Empty string equals NULL (famous quirk). Concatenation with ||. SYSDATE/SYSTIMESTAMP. DUAL table for SELECT without FROM. Pagination: FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY (12c+) or ROWNUM.
when_to_use: Existing Oracle estates and PL/SQL codebases
Workloads where downtime cost dwarfs license cost
when_not_to_use: Simple apps — operational overhead is real

install.linux: Download RPMs from oracle.com/database (Oracle Linux recommended)
install.cloud: Oracle Cloud Always Free: 2 autonomous databases

provenance: Public record of a real database engine; facts fact-checked against vendor documentation.

title: CockroachDB
overview: CockroachDB is a distributed SQL database that survives datacenter failures like a cockroach survives everything. It speaks the PostgreSQL wire protocol, so most Postgres apps connect unchanged, while data is automatically replicated and rebalanced across regions with serializable transactions.

demo.how_to_run: cockroach sql --insecure < demo.sql  (or use the built-in DB Console at :8080)

features: Survives node/zone/region loss with zero operator action
Multi-region: pin data near users, global tables
dialect_notes: PostgreSQL dialect subset: SERIAL, RETURNING, :: casts all work. Some Postgres features (certain extensions, stored procedures) are limited. Cockroach-specific: REGIONAL BY ROW tables, follower reads (AS OF SYSTEM TIME).
when_to_use: Global apps needing always-on writes in many regions
Postgres apps that must survive zone failure
when_not_to_use: Single-region small app — plain Postgres is simpler

install.linux: Download the binary tarball from cockroachlabs.com

provenance: Public record of a real database engine; facts fact-checked against vendor documentation.

title: YugabyteDB
overview: YugabyteDB is a distributed SQL database built on a Google-Spanner-inspired architecture: DocDB storage under a PostgreSQL-compatible query layer (YSQL), plus a Cassandra-compatible API (YCQL). It targets planet-scale transactional apps that still want familiar Postgres SQL.

demo.how_to_run: ysqlsh -h localhost -p 5433 -f demo.sql

features: YCQL Cassandra-compatible API on the same cluster
dialect_notes: YSQL follows PostgreSQL: SERIAL, RETURNING, :: casts. Some Postgres extensions and features (e.g. certain advisory locks, large objects) differ. YCQL is CQL-flavored for wide-column access patterns.
when_to_use: Postgres workloads that outgrow one server
Geo-distributed apps with low-latency local reads
Teams wanting one cluster for SQL + Cassandra-style access
when_not_to_use: Heavy reliance on exotic Postgres extensions

install.docker: docker run -d --name yb -p 5433:5433 -p 9042:9042 yugabytedb/yugabyte:latest bin/yugabyted start --background=false

provenance: Public record of a real database engine; facts fact-checked against vendor documentation.

title: TiDB
overview: TiDB is a distributed HTAP database that looks like MySQL to your application — same protocol, same SQL — while transparently scaling out across nodes and running analytics (TiFlash columnar engine) on live transactional data. Built for MySQL shops that hit the single-server wall.

demo.how_to_run: mysql -h 127.0.0.1 -P 4000 -u root < demo.sql  (TiDB speaks the MySQL protocol)

features: MySQL protocol compatible — migrate with existing tools
Scales reads and writes horizontally, online
TiFlash columnar replica for real-time HTAP analytics
dialect_notes: MySQL dialect: AUTO_INCREMENT, backticks, LIMIT. TiDB-specific: AUTO_RANDOM for distributed PKs (avoids hotspots), SHARD_ROW_ID_BITS, placement rules (PLACEMENT POLICY), TTL tables.
when_to_use: MySQL app that needs horizontal scale without sharding pain
Real-time analytics on live order/inventory data
when_not_to_use: You need stored procedures — TiDB support is limited
provenance: Public record of a real database engine; facts fact-checked against vendor documentation.

title: ClickHouse
overview: ClickHouse is the open-source columnar database built for blazing analytical queries over billions of rows. It compresses data hard, vectorizes execution, and answers aggregation queries in milliseconds where row stores would take minutes. The default choice for logs, metrics, and product analytics.

demo.how_to_run: clickhouse-client --multiquery < demo.sql

features: MergeTree engine family: TTL, partitioning, replication
Real-time inserts at millions of rows/sec
SQL dialect tuned for analytics, rich function library
dialect_notes: CREATE TABLE ... ENGINE = MergeTree() ORDER BY (...). Types like DateTime64, LowCardinality(String). Functions: toDate, quantile, groupArray. Joins work but star-schema denormalization is idiomatic. Not for row-by-row OLTP.
when_to_use: Product analytics replacing a slow warehouse
when_not_to_use: Transactional OLTP with frequent single-row updates
You need full ACID across tables

install.debian_ubuntu: sudo apt install clickhouse-server clickhouse-client  (via clickhouse apt repo)

provenance: Public record of a real database engine; facts fact-checked against vendor documentation.

title: DuckDB
overview: DuckDB is "SQLite for analytics": an embedded, in-process OLAP database that runs inside your Python/R/Node app and chews through Parquet and CSV files at shocking speed. No server, no setup — just import and query. It has become the default engine for local data science.

demo.how_to_run: duckdb shop.duckdb < demo.sql  (or run inside Python with duckdb.connect())

platforms: Embedded library: Python, R, Node, Java, WASM, CLI
features: In-process: zero server, queries run inside your app
Reads Parquet/CSV/JSON directly — no loading step
Full SQL: window functions, CTEs, PIVOT
MotherDuck cloud companion; spatial + httpfs extensions
dialect_notes: Postgres-flavored SQL. FROM can point at files: FROM 'data/*.parquet'. COPY (SELECT ...) TO 'out.parquet'. PIVOT/UNPIVOT built in. Structs, lists, and JSON operators; := assignment in SELECT. Sequences and auto-increment supported.
when_to_use: Local analytics in notebooks and scripts
Replacing pandas for big local files

install.cli: Download the CLI binary from duckdb.org

provenance: Public record of a real database engine; facts fact-checked against vendor documentation.

title: TimescaleDB
overview: TimescaleDB turns PostgreSQL into a time-series powerhouse via hypertables — tables automatically partitioned by time that still look and query like normal Postgres tables. IoT, metrics, and financial tick data get 10-100x ingest/query wins while keeping full SQL and the Postgres ecosystem.

demo.how_to_run: psql -h localhost -U postgres -f demo.sql

features: Hypertables: automatic time partitioning, normal SQL interface
Retention policies: drop old chunks automatically
Runs as a Postgres extension — keep your tools
dialect_notes: Standard PostgreSQL SQL plus: SELECT create_hypertable('t','ts'). Time functions: time_bucket('1 hour', ts). Continuous aggregates: CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW ... WITH (timescaledb.continuous). Chunk exclusion is automatic.
when_to_use: Any time-stamped data at volume in Postgres

install.debian_ubuntu: Add the Timescale apt repo, then: sudo apt install timescaledb-2-postgresql-18

provenance: Public record of a real database engine; facts fact-checked against vendor documentation.

title: Amazon Aurora
overview: Amazon Aurora is AWS’s cloud-native relational database, compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL, with storage that automatically grows to 128 TB and replicates six ways across availability zones. It trades operational burden for an AWS bill: no servers to manage, continuous backup, and fast failover.

demo.how_to_run: psql -h <cluster-endpoint> -U admin -f demo.sql

features: Continuous backup to S3, point-in-time restore
Aurora Serverless v2: scales to zero-ish automatically
dialect_notes: Pick your edition: Aurora MySQL speaks MySQL dialect (AUTO_INCREMENT, backticks); Aurora PostgreSQL speaks Postgres (SERIAL, RETURNING). Additions: aurora_replica_status(), fast DDL, Global Database write forwarding.
when_to_use: Startups that refuse to run database servers
when_not_to_use: Predictable tiny budgets — watch I/O charges (Standard edition)
provenance: Public record of a real database engine; facts fact-checked against vendor documentation.

title: Google Cloud Spanner
overview: Cloud Spanner is Google’s globally distributed relational database — the system behind AdWords billing — offering external-consistency transactions across continents. It gives you real SQL and ACID at planetary scale, at a price point that filters out hobby projects.

demo.how_to_run: gcloud spanner databases execute-sql mydb --instance=my-inst --sql="$(cat demo.sql)"

features: Globally distributed ACID with TrueTime external consistency
Interleaved tables: parent/child locality for fast joins
dialect_notes: GoogleSQL dialect (or PG interface): INTERLEAVE IN PARENT for co-located rows. No sequences — use bit-reversed positive sequences. Query with STRUCTs/ARRAYs. Stale reads: SELECT ... /*@ read_timestamp */ for bounded staleness.
when_to_use: Global financial/ledger workloads needing real ACID
Multi-region apps that cannot tolerate split-brain
when_not_to_use: Single-region CRUD app — overkill and overpriced
provenance: Public record of a real database engine; facts fact-checked against vendor documentation.

title: AlloyDB for PostgreSQL
overview: AlloyDB is Google’s PostgreSQL-compatible database aimed at demanding enterprise workloads: it keeps the Postgres interface developers love while adding a faster storage engine, columnar acceleration for analytics, and deep Vertex AI integration for vector search.

demo.how_to_run: psql -h <alloydb-ip> -U postgres -f demo.sql

features: 2x+ faster transactional throughput vs stock Postgres
Columnar engine for real-time HTAP analytics
Built-in pgvector + Vertex AI embeddings integration
dialect_notes: Standard PostgreSQL dialect: SERIAL/IDENTITY, RETURNING, :: casts, CTEs, window functions. AlloyDB additions: columnar engine hints, google_ml_integration for embeddings, optimized pgvector indexing.
when_to_use: Postgres workloads needing more throughput on GCP
HTAP: transactions + analytics on one cluster
AI apps needing vector search beside relational data
provenance: Public record of a real database engine; facts fact-checked against vendor documentation.

title: Snowflake
overview: Snowflake is the cloud data warehouse that separated storage from compute and made warehouses elastic: spin up a warehouse in seconds, pay per second, share data without copying it. Its semi-structured VARIANT type made JSON a first-class citizen in SQL analytics.

demo.how_to_run: snowsql -f demo.sql  (or paste into a Snowflake worksheet)

features: Elastic compute: independent scaling, per-second billing
dialect_notes: Snowflake SQL: VARIANT for JSON, FLATTEN() to explode arrays, : and . for semi-structured access (payload:customer:id). SAMPLE, QUALIFY (filter on window functions), ILIKE. No indexes — micro-partitions + clustering keys instead.
when_to_use: Teams wanting SQL analytics without infra

install.signup: Sign up at snowflake.com for a trial

provenance: Public record of a real database engine; facts fact-checked against vendor documentation.

title: Google BigQuery
overview: BigQuery is Google’s serverless data warehouse: point it at petabytes and pay per query, with no servers, no indexes, and no capacity planning. Its Standard SQL with STRUCTs and ARRAYs handles nested data natively, and BigQuery ML runs models inside SQL.

demo.how_to_run: bq query < demo.sql  (or paste into the BigQuery console)

features: Serverless: zero ops, scales to petabytes automatically
BigQuery ML: ML models in SQL
dialect_notes: Standard SQL: STRUCT<>, ARRAY<>, UNNEST() to explode. Backtick project.dataset.table names. _PARTITIONTIME pseudo-columns. QUALIFY for window-function filtering. DDL: CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE. ML: CREATE MODEL ... OPTIONS(model_type='linear_reg').

install.gcloud: gcloud alpha bq datasets create myds  (or: bq mk myds)

provenance: Public record of a real database engine; facts fact-checked against vendor documentation.

title: Amazon Redshift
overview: Amazon Redshift is AWS’s veteran MPP data warehouse, now with serverless and RA3 nodes that separate storage from compute. It speaks PostgreSQL-flavored SQL and shines for structured BI workloads already living in the AWS ecosystem.

demo.how_to_run: psql -h <redshift-endpoint> -U admin -d dev -f demo.sql

features: MPP architecture: queries parallelized across nodes
RA3: managed storage separated from compute
Redshift Spectrum: query S3 data in place
dialect_notes: Postgres 8-based dialect: DISTSTYLE/DISTKEY and SORTKEY on CREATE TABLE. No SERIAL — use IDENTITY(1,1). No tablespaces, no CREATE INDEX (use sort keys). STL/SVL system views. COPY from S3 for bulk loads.

install.aws_cli: aws redshift create-cluster --cluster-identifier mywh --node-type ra3.xlplus --master-username admin --master-user-password <pw>

provenance: Public record of a real database engine; facts fact-checked against vendor documentation.

title: Azure SQL Database
overview: Azure SQL Database is Microsoft’s managed SQL Server in the cloud — the same T-SQL engine, minus the servers. Hyperscale separates compute and storage for huge databases, and serverless tiers pause billing when idle. Natural home for .NET apps on Azure.

demo.how_to_run: sqlcmd -S myserver.database.windows.net -U admin -d mydb -i demo.sql

features: Full T-SQL compatibility with SQL Server
Hyperscale: up to 100 TB with fast scaling
Serverless tier auto-pauses to save cost
Elastic pools share resources across databases
dialect_notes: T-SQL: IDENTITY(1,1), [brackets], TOP/OFFSET-FETCH, GETDATE(), ISNULL(). Azure additions: AT TIME ZONE, JSON functions, ledger tables (tamper-evident), external tables over storage. Some on-prem features (CLR, cross-db queries) limited by tier.
when_to_use: SQL Server workloads moving to PaaS
when_not_to_use: Predictable heavy use where SQL MI fits better

install.az_cli: az sql db create --resource-group rg --server myserver --name mydb --service-objective S0

provenance: Public record of a real database engine; facts fact-checked against vendor documentation.

title: PlanetScale
overview: PlanetScale is serverless MySQL built on Vitess (YouTube’s sharding layer): branches like git, non-blocking schema changes, and scale-to-zero pricing. Developers get MySQL compatibility with a modern workflow — branch a database per pull request.

demo.how_to_run: mysql --ssl-mode=REQUIRED -h <host> -u <user> -p<password> < demo.sql  (use the PlanetScale connection string)

features: Database branching: schema changes on branches, then deploy
dialect_notes: MySQL dialect with Vitess constraints: no FOREIGN KEY enforcement across shards (use application logic), no stored procedures, limited XA. AUTO_INCREMENT works; prefer UUIDs at scale. Use the pscale CLI for branches.
when_to_use: MySQL apps wanting git-like DB workflows

install.pscale_cli: brew install planetscale/tap/pscale  (then: pscale auth login)
install.connect: Use the provided mysql:// connection string

provenance: Public record of a real database engine; facts fact-checked against vendor documentation.

title: Neon
overview: Neon is serverless PostgreSQL with storage and compute separated: databases branch instantly, scale to zero when idle, and copy-on-write clones make dev/test databases nearly free. Plain Postgres wire protocol — your existing tools just work.

demo.how_to_run: psql "<neon-connection-string>" -f demo.sql

features: True serverless Postgres: scale to zero
dialect_notes: Standard PostgreSQL dialect: SERIAL/IDENTITY, RETURNING, :: casts, CTEs, JSONB. Neon additions are operational (branching via API/console), not SQL — your queries are vanilla Postgres.
when_to_use: Preview databases per PR via branching
when_not_to_use: You need exotic extensions not yet supported

install.connect: Use the pooled connection string from the dashboard

provenance: Public record of a real database engine; facts fact-checked against vendor documentation.

title: Supabase
overview: Supabase is the open-source Firebase alternative built on PostgreSQL: instant REST and realtime APIs over your Postgres tables, plus auth, storage, and edge functions. You get a real database you can also reach with plain SQL — no lock-in to a proprietary API.

demo.how_to_run: Paste into the Supabase dashboard SQL editor, or: psql "<connection-string>" -f demo.sql

features: Postgres with auto-generated REST + GraphQL APIs
Row-level security as the auth model
dialect_notes: Full PostgreSQL dialect. Supabase conventions: RLS policies (CREATE POLICY), auth.uid() in policies, storage.objects for files, realtime publication for live tables. Otherwise vanilla Postgres SQL.
when_to_use: MVPs needing backend in an afternoon
Apps wanting Postgres plus realtime/auth without building it
when_not_to_use: Complex multi-service backends — still just Postgres underneath

install.cloud: Sign up at supabase.com > New project
install.self_host: git clone supabase/supabase && docker compose up (see self-hosting guide)

provenance: Public record of a real database engine; facts fact-checked against vendor documentation.

title: H2 Database Engine
overview: H2 is a fast, embeddable Java SQL database — the go-to for Java apps, tests, and teaching. It runs in-process, in-memory, or as a small server, and its compatibility modes emulate other dialects for testing.

demo.how_to_run: Paste into the H2 web console (jdbc:h2:~/shop), or run via your Java app

platforms: Any JVM: embedded, in-memory, or server mode
features: Compatibility modes: PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle, MSSQL
dialect_notes: Standard SQL plus compatibility modes (MODE=PostgreSQL etc.). AUTO_INCREMENT or IDENTITY for generated keys. Sequences supported. In-memory URL: jdbc:h2:mem:test. Functions vary by mode — test in your target mode.
when_to_use: Embedded storage in Java desktop apps
Prototyping before choosing a server DB

install.jar: Download h2-*.jar from h2database.com; java -jar h2-*.jar opens the console

provenance: Public record of a real database engine; facts fact-checked against vendor documentation.

title: Firebird
overview: Firebird is a mature open-source RDBMS born from Borland InterBase, famous for running embedded inside applications with a tiny footprint and for its rock-solid stored procedures and triggers. A quiet workhorse in point-of-sale and industrial software.

demo.how_to_run: isql-fb shop.fdb < demo.sql  (or paste into FlameRobin / DBeaver)

features: Embedded or server from the same engine
dialect_notes: Classic InterBase dialect: generators (CREATE GENERATOR) + triggers for auto-increment (or GENERATED ... AS IDENTITY in v3+). FIRST n / SKIP m for pagination (or OFFSET/FETCH). Concatenation with ||. DATE/TIMESTAMP types; BOOLEAN added in v3.
when_to_use: POS and industrial systems needing reliability
when_not_to_use: You need a giant ecosystem of tools

install.embedded: Ship fbembed.dll / libfbembed.so with your app

provenance: Public record of a real database engine; facts fact-checked against vendor documentation.

title: Percona Server for MySQL
overview: Percona Server for MySQL is a drop-in, performance-tuned replacement for MySQL with extra instrumentation (including the free Percona Monitoring and Management). It adds enterprise-grade backup (XtraBackup) and diagnostics while staying 100% protocol-compatible.

demo.how_to_run: mysql -u root -p < demo.sql

features: 100% MySQL drop-in: same protocol, same data files
Enhanced audit, thread pool, and metrics
TokuDB-era lessons folded into InnoDB tuning
dialect_notes: Identical to MySQL dialect: AUTO_INCREMENT, backticks, LIMIT. Percona additions are operational: extra INFORMATION_SCHEMA tables, SHOW ENGINE INNODB STATUS extensions, backup history tables. Your SQL needs no changes.
when_to_use: MySQL in production wanting better observability
Free hot backups without enterprise licenses
when_not_to_use: You want a different engine, not a better MySQL

install.debian_ubuntu: Add the Percona apt repo, then: sudo apt install percona-server-server
install.pmm: Deploy Percona Monitoring and Management for dashboards

provenance: Public record of a real database engine; facts fact-checked against vendor documentation.
